messages:
Priya (Platform): Hey team — we want to onboard Sentry for the new support app (ops-support). Quick ask: can we send full request/response payloads to Sentry or do we need to redact first?
Maya (Eng-Security): short answer: redact. Long answer: anything that might contain PII (emails, phone numbers, auth headers, JWTs, credit card numbers) must not be forwarded. We need a data-classification + redaction plan before vendor onboarding. :+1:
Priya (Platform): understood. Is there an approved redaction regex or config we can reuse?
Maya (Eng-Security): yes — use the org standard redaction middleware. Example we usually push upstream to the SDK before sending:
```
const redactionRules = [
  { key: /email|user_email/i, redact: true },
  { key: /authorization|auth_token/i, redact: true },
  { pattern: /\b[0-9]{12,19}\b/, redact: 'REDACTED_CC' }, // cc-like numbers
  { pattern: /\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}\b/, redact: 'REDACTED_EMAIL' }
];
// apply before Sentry.captureException / captureMessage
```
Maya (Eng-Security): also ensure we trim full request bodies — only include headers+path+error message plus sanitized context for debugging.
Jonah (SRE): for SRE access, prefer a scoped API token with read-only events and project-level scope. Do NOT give vendor account owner or full org access. If Sentry supports SAML provisioning, prefer SCIM/SAML and SCIM-only for user sync.
Alex (DevEx): will the DevEx team need to share session replay (FullStory) data as well? If so, that's a separate risk review — session replay can be high risk for PII exposure.
Priya (Platform): not planning session replay, just errors + breadcrumb traces.
Maya (Eng-Security): good. Next steps: 1) fill access request form (https://internal.company/forms/vendor-access) 2) attach data flow diagram + example payloads 3) list retention/retention policy (we prefer 30-90d) 4) legal review for DPA if data leaves region.
Priya (Platform): who signs off after we attach items?
Maya (Eng-Security): Eng-Security + Platform lead + Legal if DPA/PII involved. For scoped tokens we can approve without Legal if no PII and data stays in-region.
Priya (Platform): example log line we plan to send: ```{ userId: 12345, path: '/api/v1/login', err: 'TypeError at auth.js:42', body: { email: 'user@example.com', password: '***' } }``` — should we scrub userId too?
Maya (Eng-Security): userId can be kept if it's internal non-identifying id; if it maps to real user profile with email, treat as PI. Prefer hashed user_id (sha256) and no raw emails. e.g., user_hash = sha256(userId + salt).
Jonah (SRE): add to ops checklist: enable audit logs in Sentry + tie to our KMS for token rotation, set token TTL 90 days, and restrict IPs to our VPC egress ranges if possible.
Priya (Platform): noted. Any special config for Sentry DSNs?
Maya (Eng-Security): never hardcode DSNs in repos. Use secrets manager and reference via runtime env. Also enable sample rate < 1 for production if traffic noisy.
Alex (DevEx): I can open the vendor onboarding ticket and loop Legal if needed. Should I request a vendor questionnaire?
Maya (Eng-Security): yes — vendor security questionnaire recommended for external SaaS. Also request SOC2 / ISO docs if they claim.
LegalBot: Automated: created vendor-review ticket #VR-2789 and assigned to Legal & Eng-Security. Link: https://internal.tracker/VR-2789
Priya (Platform): thanks all — I'll prepare the data flow + sanitized example payloads and add the hashed-user-id approach. Will post back when the form is filled. :raised_hands:
Maya (Eng-Security): thanks — ping me when you attach the examples, I'll do a quick redaction QA. :eyes:
